item.title: Central North Pacific Tropical Weather Outlook
item.description:
000
ACPN50 PHFO 260531
TWOCP

Tropical Weather Outlook
NWS Central Pacific Hurricane Center Honolulu HI
Issued by NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL
800 PM HST Tue Aug 25 2026

For the central North Pacific...between 140W and 180W:

Active Systems:
The National Hurricane Center is issuing advisories on Tropical
Storm Lala, located several hundred miles north of Kure Atoll, and
on Tropical Storm Iselle, located well to the west of the southern
tip of the Baja California Peninsula.

Western East Pacific:
A weak, elongated area of low pressure located well to the
east-southeast of the Hawaiian Islands is producing disorganized
showers and thunderstorms. Environmental conditions appear conducive
for gradual development of this system, and a tropical depression is
likely to form late this week or early this weekend while the system
drifts to the northeast, then turns westward.
* Formation chance through 48 hours...medium...40 percent.
* Formation chance through 7 days...high...70 percent.

Central Pacific:
An area of low pressure could form well south of the Hawaiian
Islands late this week or over the weekend. Some gradual development
is possible by early next week while the system moves slowly
west-northwestward, well south-southwest of the Hawaiian Islands.
* Formation chance through 48 hours...low...near 0 percent.
* Formation chance through 7 days...low...20 percent.

$$
Forecaster Reinhart
NNNN

item.description:
Issued at 1100 PM HST Tue Aug 25 2026 
565 
WTPA32 PHFO 260834
TCPCP2
 
BULLETIN
Tropical Storm Lala Advisory Number  56
NWS Central Pacific Hurricane Center Honolulu HI   CP012026
Issued by NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL
1100 PM HST Tue Aug 25 2026
 
...LALA WEAKENS...
 
 
SUMMARY OF 1100 PM HST...0900 UTC...INFORMATION
-----------------------------------------------
LOCATION...35.4N 177.7W
ABOUT 555 MI...895 KM N OF PEARL AND HERMES ATOLL
ABOUT 485 MI...780 KM N OF KURE ATOLL
MAXIMUM SUSTAINED WINDS...45 MPH...75 KM/H
PRESENT MOVEMENT...NW OR 310 DEGREES AT 5 MPH...7 KM/H
MINIMUM CENTRAL PRESSURE...997 MB...29.44 INCHES
 
 
WATCHES AND WARNINGS
--------------------
There are no coastal watches or warnings in effect.
 
 
DISCUSSION AND OUTLOOK
----------------------
At 1100 PM HST (0900 UTC), the center of Tropical Storm Lala was 
located near latitude 35.4 North, longitude 177.7 West. Lala is 
moving toward the northwest near 5 mph (7 km/h), and a slow 
northwestward motion is expected to continue over the next couple of 
days.
 
Maximum sustained winds are near 45 mph (75 km/h) with higher gusts. 
Gradual weakening is expected during the next couple of days, and 
Lala is forecast to become a post-tropical cyclone by late Thursday.
 
Tropical-storm-force winds extend outward up to 115 miles (185 km)
from the center.
 
The estimated minimum central pressure is 997 mb (29.44 inches).
 
 
HAZARDS AFFECTING LAND
----------------------
None.
 
 
NEXT ADVISORY
-------------
Next complete advisory at 500 AM HST.
 
$$
Forecaster Reinhart

item.title: Tropical Storm Lala Forecast Discussion Number 56
item.description:
Issued at 1100 PM HST Tue Aug 25 2026 
621 
WTPA42 PHFO 260835
TCDCP2
 
Tropical Storm Lala Discussion Number  56
NWS Central Pacific Hurricane Center Honolulu HI   CP012026
Issued by NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL
1100 PM HST Tue Aug 25 2026
 
The satellite presentation of Lala has slowly deteriorated tonight. 
Water vapor imagery shows some drier air has worked its way into the 
circulation, which has led to diminished convection and warming 
infrared cloud tops near and around the center. The Dvorak current 
intensity estimates from JTWC and HFO have decreased to T2.5/35 kt, 
and so the initial intensity is lowered to 40 kt.

Fixes from recent AMSR3 and GMI passive microwave images suggest 
Lala has resumed a slow northwestward motion (310/4 kt), steered by 
a mid-level ridge just to the northeast of the storm. This ridge 
should keep Lala on a slow northwestward heading while the storm 
approaches the International Date Line (IDL). The updated NHC track 
forecast has been nudged to the right of the previous one, in 
response to an eastward shift in the latest track guidance envelope. 
Lala will remain in a fairly dry mid-level environment while 
encountering increasing shear over cool waters during the next 
couple of days. Thus, continued weakening is forecast, and Lala is 
predicted to lose organized convection and become a post-tropical 
low by 48 h as it reaches the IDL. Post-tropical Lala is forecast to 
accelerate deeper into the mid-latitudes over the weekend, and it 
should open up into a trough over the northern Pacific by 120 h.
 
 
FORECAST POSITIONS AND MAX WINDS
